name: Semiconductor physics and semiconductor devices
summary: Doped silicon, III-V and wide-gap semiconductors are one object seen twice: condensed matter supplies gaps, mobilities, recombination and junction physics; device physics turns them into MOSFETs, LEDs, lasers and photovoltaics.
sources: Bardeen & Brattain (1948). "The Transistor, A Semi-Conductor Triode". *Phys. Rev.* 74, 230. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.74.230](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.74.230)
Shockley & Queisser (1961). "Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells". *J. Appl. Phys.* 32, 510. [doi:10.1063/1.1736034](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1736034)

name: Graphene nanopores for single-molecule sensing
summary: A single graphene layer is thinner than the spacing of DNA bases, so ionic current through a graphene nanopore resolves translocating molecules with sub-nanometre thickness, a step toward solid-state sequencing.
sources: Garaj et al. (2010). "Graphene as a subnanometre trans-electrode membrane". *Nature* 467, 190. [arXiv:1006.3518](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.3518)

name: Quantum-dot light emitters and photovoltaics
summary: Size-tuned colloidal and perovskite nanocrystals are used in displays (QLEDs), downconverters and solar cells; confinement sets the emission colour and multiple-exciton generation offers a route past the Shockley-Queisser limit.
sources: Murray, Norris & Bawendi (1993). "Synthesis and characterization of nearly monodisperse CdE (E = sulfur, selenium, tellurium) semiconductor nanocrystallites". *J. Am. Chem. Soc.* 115, 8706. [doi:10.1021/ja00072a025](https://doi.org/10.1021/ja00072a025)

name: Two-dimensional semiconductor channels for transistors
summary: Monolayer MoS2 and related TMDs provide atomically thin channels with sizeable gaps, immune to short-channel effects that limit silicon scaling; contact resistance and dielectric integration are the open device problems.
sources: Radisavljevic et al. (2011). "Single-layer MoS2 transistors". *Nat. Nanotechnol.* 6, 147. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2010.279](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2010.279)

name: NV magnetometry imaging of 2D magnets
summary: Scanning single-spin (NV) magnetometry images stray fields of atomically thin magnets such as CrI3 quantitatively, resolving layer-dependent magnetization and domains; it is now a standard probe of 2D magnetism and spin textures.
sources: Thiel et al. (2019). "Probing magnetism in 2D materials at the nanoscale with single-spin microscopy". *Science* 364, 973. [arXiv:1902.01406](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.01406)

name: Crackling noise: Barkhausen jumps and earthquakes
summary: Barkhausen noise from domain-wall avalanches in ferromagnets and earthquakes on faults both show power-law size distributions explained by depinning of an elastic interface in a random medium, the 'crackling noise' universality family.
breaks: Fault systems have long-range elastic interactions, healing and inertia that can produce characteristic quakes; universality-class assignments and exponents differ, and magnetic avalanches are tuned by an external field rather than tectonic loading.
sources: Sethna, Dahmen & Myers (2001). "Crackling noise". *Nature* 410, 242. [arXiv:cond-mat/0102091](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0102091)

name: Rock magnetism and the paleomagnetic record
summary: Remanent magnetization of magnetite-bearing rocks, explained by Neel's theory of thermally activated single-domain grains, records the geomagnetic field; stripes of reversed magnetization on the sea floor confirmed sea-floor spreading and plate tectonics.
sources: Vine & Matthews (1963). "Magnetic Anomalies Over Oceanic Ridges". *Nature* 199, 947. [doi:10.1038/199947a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/199947a0)

name: Spintronic memory and read heads in electronics
summary: Giant and tunnelling magnetoresistance moved from discovery to hard-disk read heads within a decade, and spin-transfer-torque MRAM is now embedded in CMOS logic processes as non-volatile memory.
sources: Baibich et al. (1988). "Giant Magnetoresistance of (001)Fe/(001)Cr Magnetic Superlattices". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 61, 2472. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2472](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2472)

name: Soft-matter physics of biological materials
summary: Membranes, biopolymers, gels and cytoskeletal networks have energies of order k_BT, so entropic elasticity, fluctuations, self-assembly and viscoelasticity, the core of soft matter, set the mechanics of cells and biomolecules.
sources: de Gennes (1992). "Soft matter". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 64, 645. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.64.645](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.64.645)

name: Cells and tissues as active matter
summary: The actomyosin cortex and epithelial tissues are active gels and active nematics; topological defects in epithelial monolayers localize stress and trigger cell extrusion, the same +1/2 defect physics as in microtubule active nematics.
sources: Marchetti et al. (2013). "Hydrodynamics of soft active matter". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 85, 1143. [arXiv:1207.2929](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.2929)
Saw et al. (2017). "Topological defects in epithelia govern cell death and extrusion". *Nature* 544, 212. [doi:10.1038/nature21718](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature21718)

name: Flocking theory and collective animal behaviour
summary: Vicsek and Toner-Tu theories of polar active matter describe starling flocks, fish schools and bacterial swarms; field data showing starlings interact with a fixed number of topological neighbours fed back into active-matter models.
sources: Vicsek et al. (1995). "Novel Type of Phase Transition in a System of Self-Driven Particles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 1226. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226)

Ballerini et al. (2008). "Interaction ruling animal collective behavior depends on topological rather than metric distance: Evidence from a field study". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 105, 1232. [arXiv:0709.1916](https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1916)

name: Brownian colloids as force probes
summary: Optical and magnetic tweezers are calibrated by the Brownian motion of a trapped colloidal bead: equipartition and the Lorentzian power spectrum with Stokes drag give the trap stiffness that turns position into force.

name: Granular friction and earthquake faults
summary: Fault gouge is a sheared granular layer: rate-and-state friction, stick-slip instability, dilatancy and shear localization measured on granular materials explain earthquake nucleation and aftershock behaviour.
sources: Marone (1998). "Laboratory-derived friction laws and their application to seismic faulting". *Annu. Rev. Earth Planet. Sci.* 26, 643. [doi:10.1146/annurev.earth.26.1.643](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.earth.26.1.643)

name: Phase-change glasses for non-volatile memory
summary: Chalcogenide glasses such as Ge2Sb2Te5 switch in nanoseconds between amorphous and crystalline states with very different resistivity and reflectivity; crystallization kinetics and glass stability are the device physics of phase-change memory.
sources: Wuttig & Yamada (2007). "Phase-change materials for rewriteable data storage". *Nat. Mater.* 6, 824. [doi:10.1038/nmat2009](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmat2009)

name: Jamming and unjamming of biological tissues
summary: Confluent epithelia undergo a rigidity (jamming) transition controlled by cell shape rather than density, analogous to athermal jamming; unjammed, fluid-like tissue is linked to wound healing, asthma and cancer invasion.
sources: Bi et al. (2015). "A density-independent rigidity transition in biological tissues". *Nat. Phys.* 11, 1074. [arXiv:1409.0593](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0593)

name: Rugged energy landscapes: glasses and protein folding
summary: Random-energy and spin-glass landscape ideas developed for glass formers were applied to proteins, giving the folding funnel and the principle of minimal frustration: foldable sequences have a folding temperature well above their glass temperature.
sources: Bryngelson & Wolynes (1987). "Spin glasses and the statistical mechanics of protein folding". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 84, 7524. [doi:10.1073/pnas.84.21.7524](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.84.21.7524)

name: Helfrich elasticity: from liquid crystals to membranes
summary: Lipid bilayers are two-dimensional smectic-A liquid crystals; Helfrich, co-inventor of the twisted-nematic display, transferred Frank curvature elasticity to membranes, giving the bending energy that predicts red-blood-cell shapes and vesicle fluctuations.
sources: Helfrich (1973). "Elastic Properties of Lipid Bilayers: Theory and Possible Experiments". *Z. Naturforsch. C* 28, 693. [doi:10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209](https://doi.org/10.1515/znc-1973-11-1209)

name: Proteins and nucleic acids as polymers
summary: Polymer physics (random walks, excluded volume, theta collapse, persistence length) gives the baseline for unfolded proteins and DNA; folding is a heteropolymer collapse with sequence-specific interactions.
sources: Flory (1949). "The Configuration of Real Polymer Chains". *J. Chem. Phys.* 17, 303. [doi:10.1063/1.1747243](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1747243)

name: Flory-Huggins phase separation and biomolecular condensates
summary: Membraneless organelles (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules) form by liquid-liquid phase separation of multivalent proteins and RNA, described with Flory-Huggins polymer-solution theory and its sticker-spacer extensions.
sources: Brangwynne et al. (2009). "Germline P Granules Are Liquid Droplets That Localize by Controlled Dissolution/Condensation". *Science* 324, 1729. [doi:10.1126/science.1172046](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1172046)

Hyman, Weber & Jülicher (2014). "Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation in Biology". *Annu. Rev. Cell Dev. Biol.* 30, 39. [doi:10.1146/annurev-cellbio-100913-013325](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-cellbio-100913-013325)

name: Worm-like chain elasticity of single DNA molecules
summary: Force-extension curves of single DNA molecules in optical and magnetic tweezers are fitted by the worm-like-chain model of semiflexible polymers, giving a 50 nm persistence length and confirming entropic elasticity at the single-molecule level.
sources: Bustamante et al. (1994). "Entropic elasticity of λ-phage DNA". *Science* 265, 1599. [doi:10.1126/science.8079175](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.8079175)

name: DMRG, QMC and coupled cluster across fields
summary: DMRG, invented for 1D spin chains, became a leading method for strongly correlated molecules (active spaces of transition-metal clusters), while coupled cluster and quantum Monte Carlo moved from nuclear and quantum chemistry into solids; agreement across methods is the benchmark standard in both fields.
sources: Chan & Sharma (2011). "The Density Matrix Renormalization Group in Quantum Chemistry". *Annu. Rev. Phys. Chem.* 62, 465. [doi:10.1146/annurev-physchem-032210-103338](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-physchem-032210-103338)

name: Superconductors in accelerators
summary: Accelerators are the largest users of applied superconductivity: NbTi and Nb3Sn dipoles and quadrupoles bend and focus beams, and superconducting niobium RF cavities provide high-gradient, low-loss acceleration.

name: BCS surface resistance of SRF cavities
summary: Niobium superconducting RF cavities are limited by the BCS surface resistance from thermally excited quasiparticles, plus residual losses from trapped flux; nitrogen doping and Nb3Sn coatings are gap-engineering responses that raise Q0 and gradient.

name: Superconducting magnets for MRI
summary: Clinical MRI scanners use persistent-mode NbTi solenoids at 1.5-7 T; type-II superconductivity with strong flux pinning gives the stable, homogeneous field whose Larmor frequency sets image signal and resolution.

name: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering of cuprates
summary: High-resolution RIXS at synchrotrons measures paramagnons and charge-density-wave correlations in cuprates; it revealed incommensurate charge order competing with superconductivity in YBCO.
sources: Ghiringhelli et al. (2012). "Long-Range Incommensurate Charge Fluctuations in (Y,Nd)Ba2Cu3O6+x". *Science* 337, 821. [arXiv:1207.0915](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0915)

name: SQUID magnetometry
summary: SQUIDs turn flux quantization and Josephson interference into femtotesla magnetometers used for magnetoencephalography, geophysics, rock magnetism and condensed-matter susceptibility measurements.
sources: Hämäläinen et al. (1993). "Magnetoencephalography—theory, instrumentation, and applications to noninvasive studies of the working human brain". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 65, 413. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.65.413](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.65.413)

name: Topological origin of equatorial waves
summary: Applying Chern-number band topology to the rotating shallow-water equations shows that the equatorial Kelvin and Yanai waves are topologically protected edge modes forced by the sign change of the Coriolis parameter at the equator.
sources: Delplace, Marston & Venaille (2017). "Topological origin of equatorial waves". *Science* 358, 1075. [arXiv:1702.07583](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07583)

name: Synchrotron ARPES of topological surface states
summary: Spin- and angle-resolved photoemission with tunable synchrotron light identified the odd number of spin-momentum-locked surface Dirac cones that define 3D topological insulators, and later Fermi arcs in Weyl semimetals.
sources: Hsieh et al. (2008). "A topological Dirac insulator in a quantum spin Hall phase". *Nature* 452, 970. [arXiv:0902.1356](https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.1356)

name: Blackbody radiation and radiative equilibrium
summary: Both rest on Planck blackbody radiation and radiative transfer: the CMB is a relic thermal spectrum, Earth's climate set by balance of absorbed sunlight and outgoing thermal radiation.
breaks: The CMB is a decoupled relic freely streaming; Earth's emission is non-equilibrium and gray-body with strong absorption bands.

name: Inverse problems and tomographic reconstruction
summary: Weak-lensing mass maps and CT/MRI reconstruction are regularized linear inverse problems, using Kaiser–Squires-type inversion, Wiener filtering and sparsity priors.
breaks: Lensing has sparse noisy sampling and shape noise; CT has controlled acquisition geometry.

name: Quantum sensors for dark matter
summary: Axion and light dark-matter searches use SQUIDs, atomic magnetometers, NV centres, atomic clocks and interferometers; quantum-sensing techniques set sensitivity, including squeezing.

name: Low-background detectors and scintillation
summary: Scintillators, liquid xenon and time-of-flight photodetection developed for particle and dark-matter detection also drive PET detector design; low-noise photosensors cross over.
breaks: Dark-matter detectors require extreme radiopurity and keV thresholds; PET needs high rate at 511 keV.

name: Jets and undulator radiation
summary: Relativistic jets emit synchrotron and inverse-Compton radiation, with Doppler boosting; undulators and FELs give coherent, narrow-band versions of the same radiation by accelerated charges.
breaks: Jet emission is incoherent and broadband; FELs achieve coherence via microbunching.

name: Turbulence in stratified fluids
summary: Intracluster gas and the oceans are stratified turbulent fluids, with buoyancy-driven mixing and internal gravity waves described by Brunt–Väisälä frequency.
breaks: Cluster gas is magnetized, weakly collisional plasma with cooling and AGN feedback.

name: Statistical inference of dynamical systems
summary: Galactic archaeology and biophysical data analysis both use Bayesian inference and machine learning on large noisy catalogues; Gaia phase-space modelling parallels inference in living-systems data.
breaks: The shared element is generic statistical practice.

name: Rossby waves and density waves
summary: Both feature large-scale rotating-fluid wave patterns: Rossby waves from the beta effect in atmospheres, and spiral density waves in rotating galactic disks with differential rotation, with analogous dispersion structure.
breaks: Galactic disks are self-gravitating and collisionless stars; Rossby waves are restoring-force vorticity waves in a fluid.

name: Cosmic accelerators versus machines
summary: Diffusive shock acceleration and Fermi mechanisms are natural counterparts of laboratory accelerators; the Hillas criterion parallels the size-times-field limit on achievable energy.
breaks: Cosmic acceleration is stochastic, shock-based and power-law; machines use coherent, controlled RF fields.

name: Synchrotron radiation in nature and the lab
summary: Relativistic electrons in magnetic fields emit synchrotron radiation, identical physics in AGN jets, pulsar nebulae and storage-ring light sources, with the same critical-frequency scaling.

name: Cosmic rays and air showers in the atmosphere
summary: Cosmic rays are detected through extensive air showers developing in the atmosphere; cosmic-ray ionisation is also proposed to affect atmospheric electricity and cloud nucleation.
breaks: Cosmic-ray cloud seeding is weak and disputed.

name: Cosmic-ray and hadron-therapy interactions
summary: Heavy-ion transport, nuclear fragmentation and Bragg-peak energy loss are shared: galactic cosmic-ray shielding for astronauts uses the same codes and radiobiology as carbon-ion therapy.

name: Coherent emission from bunched charges
summary: FRB models invoke coherent curvature or maser emission from bunched charges, resembling coherent synchrotron radiation and FEL microbunching where power scales as N².
breaks: FRB coherence mechanism is unsettled; FELs rely on a known collective instability.

name: Planet spectra as molecular spectroscopy
summary: Identifying planetary atmospheric species relies on laboratory rovibrational line lists and selection rules; the same spectroscopy underlies remote sensing of planets and exoplanets.

name: Planetary climate as Earth climate physics
summary: Energy balance, greenhouse effect and feedbacks developed for Earth apply to other planets and exoplanets, setting equilibrium temperatures and habitability.

name: Physical limits of life and biosignatures
summary: Habitability asks which physical constraints (energy, chemistry, thermodynamics) permit life; physics of living systems quantifies those limits, such as energy use, noise and information processing.

name: Habitable zone from climate feedbacks
summary: Habitable-zone edges are set by radiative-convective climate physics: runaway greenhouse from water-vapour feedback and ice-albedo snowball transitions, as in Earth climate models.

name: Spectroscopic databases serve exoplanet retrievals
summary: Line lists such as HITRAN and ExoMol, from quantum-chemistry and spectroscopy, are essential inputs for interpreting JWST exoplanet spectra.

name: Transmission spectra as molecular absorption
summary: Exoplanet transmission and emission spectra are decoded using molecular line lists, cross sections and Raman/collision-induced absorption knowledge from molecular spectroscopy.

name: Greenhouse and inversion physics on other worlds
summary: Greenhouse trapping, lapse rates and temperature inversions explain exoplanet thermal structure just as they do Earth's atmosphere.

name: Radiative transfer codes from Earth to exoplanets
summary: Radiative-convective models, correlated-k opacities and general circulation models built for Earth climate are reused for exoplanet atmospheres and retrievals.
breaks: Earth-tuned assumptions (water condensation, near-1 bar) fail for hot Jupiters and non-solar compositions.

name: Astrochemistry in disks
summary: Disk chemistry and the delivery of volatiles depend on gas-phase and grain-surface reaction rates, ion-molecule kinetics and snow lines, drawing on reaction-dynamics rate theory.

name: Grain-surface chemistry and catalysis
summary: H2 formation and ice mantle chemistry on dust grains proceed via adsorption, diffusion and Langmuir–Hinshelwood reactions, the same surface-science mechanisms as in heterogeneous catalysis.
breaks: Interstellar grains are at ~10 K with quantum tunnelling, in ultra-low-density gas.

name: Rotating stratified turbulence in disks and atmospheres
summary: Protoplanetary-disk vortices, zonal flows and Rossby wave instability parallel geophysical vortices and jets in rotating shear flows; Coriolis dynamics governs both.
breaks: Disks involve magnetorotational turbulence, dust coupling and self-gravity.

name: Milankovitch cycles and orbital forcing
summary: Secular orbital perturbations change Earth's eccentricity, obliquity and precession, modulating insolation and driving glacial cycles.
breaks: Climate response is nonlinear, with ice-sheet feedbacks.

name: Neutron-star asteroseismology and crust elasticity
summary: Neutron-star crusts support shear modes and quakes analogous to earthquakes; magnetar giant-flare quasi-periodic oscillations are interpreted as crustal torsional modes, as in seismology.
breaks: Crust is a Coulomb lattice at nuclear densities with extreme magnetic fields and superfluid coupling.

name: Positron annihilation and gamma detection
summary: Positron annihilation producing 511 keV photons is used in PET and is observed in the Galactic 511 keV line; gamma-ray instrumentation overlaps with nuclear-medicine detectors, such as Compton cameras.

name: Opacities and equations of state
summary: Stellar and planetary interiors require atomic opacities and equations of state computed with electronic-structure methods, including density functional and molecular dynamics for warm dense matter.
breaks: Stellar plasmas are partially ionized at high temperature, beyond standard ground-state quantum chemistry.

name: Convection and radiative-convective structure
summary: Stellar envelopes and planetary atmospheres share Schwarzschild/lapse-rate stability criteria and mixing-length convection; the adiabatic gradient decides radiative versus convective layers.
breaks: Stars have radiation pressure, ionization and nuclear sources; atmospheres have moisture and rotation constraints.

name: Solar forcing of climate
summary: Solar luminosity, its variability and the faint young Sun set the incoming flux in Earth's energy balance; solar cycle irradiance variations give a small forcing term.

name: Dynamo theory: Sun and geodynamo
summary: Solar and geodynamo both arise from MHD induction in convecting conducting fluid, with rotation and helicity (alpha-omega effect) driving field generation and reversals.
breaks: Solar dynamo is turbulent with strong stratification and a 11-yr cycle; geodynamo has low Rossby number and the solid inner core.

name: Helioseismology and seismology inversions
summary: Both infer interior structure from observed wave modes and travel times via inversion: p-modes for the Sun, body and surface waves and normal modes for Earth. Methods and the mathematics of tomography parallel each other.
breaks: Solar modes are stochastically excited acoustic waves in a fluid; Earth has shear waves, discontinuities and sparse source locations.

name: High-pressure equations of state for planetary cores
summary: Laser-shock and diamond-anvil experiments measure iron's equation of state and melting at core pressures, calibrating seismically inferred inner-core density and temperature.

name: Charged-particle stopping power
summary: Alpha and ion energy deposition in dense plasma and Bragg-peak dose deposition in tissue both follow Bethe-type stopping physics, with plasma screening modifying stopping in hot targets.
breaks: Free-electron collective response in plasmas changes stopping relative to bound-electron tissue.

name: Laser-driven particle and radiation sources
summary: Intense lasers in plasma drive electron and ion beams and betatron or undulator-like radiation, producing compact versions of accelerator and light-source outputs.

name: Radiation by accelerated charges
summary: Betatron radiation in plasma, relativistic Thomson scattering and undulator radiation all derive from the Liénard–Liparticle radiation formula for accelerated relativistic charges.

name: Laser-driven ion acceleration for proton therapy
summary: Target-normal sheath acceleration produces MeV-scale protons from laser-irradiated foils, targeted at Bragg-peak therapy, though current energies and reproducibility fall short.

name: Accelerator physics applied to plasma acceleration
summary: Emittance, beta-function matching, energy spread and staging from conventional beam dynamics are the figures of merit for plasma-accelerated beams.

name: Plasma wakefields as compact accelerators
summary: Plasma wakefield accelerators replace RF cavities with plasma waves sustaining GV/m gradients; beam dynamics, emittance and staging concepts from accelerator physics govern their beam quality.

name: Betatron oscillations in ion channel
summary: Beam electrons in the plasma ion-channel focusing field undergo betatron oscillations with the same envelope equations as strong focusing lattices, with focusing strength set by plasma density.

name: Plasma-driven free-electron lasers
summary: Plasma-accelerated beams and betatron emission are being used to drive FELs and X-ray sources, but the FEL's tight emittance and energy-spread demands challenge plasma beams.
breaks: Plasma beams' percent-level energy spread typically exceeds the FEL Pierce parameter tolerance.

name: Compact accelerators for radiotherapy
summary: Laser-plasma ion and electron beams are proposed as compact sources for proton therapy and FLASH radiotherapy, but stability and energy spread remain limiting.

name: Plasma processing for device fabrication
summary: Plasma etching, deposition and ion implantation-related processes pattern and build transistors and solar cells; sheath physics sets ion energy and anisotropy of etched features.

name: Plasma–surface interactions and plasma catalysis
summary: Plasma radicals and ions adsorb, react and sputter at surfaces, linking discharge physics to adsorption, surface reactions and plasma-assisted catalysis.

name: Plasma medicine and biological response
summary: Cold atmospheric plasmas deliver reactive oxygen and nitrogen species to cells and tissue, so biological sensing and response physics determines therapeutic and toxic outcomes.

name: Non-equilibrium plasma chemistry and reaction kinetics
summary: Electron-impact dissociation, vibrational excitation and radical reactions in cold plasmas follow state-resolved rate theory and potential-energy-surface concepts, with electron temperature far above gas temperature.
breaks: Rate theories assuming a single Boltzmann temperature fail when electron and gas temperatures differ strongly.

name: Surface chemistry underlying plasma etching
summary: Etch and deposition rates and selectivity are set by adsorption, ion-enhanced surface reactions and sputter yields studied in surface science.

name: Neutral beam injectors as ion accelerators
summary: Neutral beam heating of fusion plasmas relies on ion source, electrostatic acceleration and neutraliser technology developed in accelerator physics.

name: Hamiltonian field-line flow and storage-ring dynamics
summary: Magnetic field lines in toroidal devices form a Hamiltonian system with islands and KAM surfaces, as do particle orbits in storage rings with nonlinear resonances.
breaks: Field-line flow has no physical particle dynamics, and rotational transform plays the role of tune.

name: Superconducting magnets and RF technology
summary: Tokamaks and accelerators share superconducting magnet technology (Nb3Sn, NbTi, HTS) and RF heating or klystron sources, with cross-fertilised cryogenics and power systems.

name: Drift waves and Rossby waves
summary: Drift waves in magnetized plasma obey the Hasegawa–Mima equation, mathematically identical to the Charney–Hasegawa–Mima quasi-geostrophic equation, with zonal flows paralleling atmospheric jets.
breaks: Plasma drift waves involve adiabatic electron response and finite Larmor radius, with no direct atmospheric counterpart.

name: Planetary dynamos in Earth science
summary: Earth's field generation and reversals are a dynamo problem in rotating convecting conducting fluid, linking geophysics to MHD dynamo theory.

name: Rotating convective flows and quasi-geostrophy
summary: Core convection under rapid rotation is Taylor–Proudman constrained, mirroring geostrophic balance and Rossby-wave dynamics in the atmosphere, with Lorentz force replacing part of the Coriolis balance.
breaks: Magnetic field and Lorentz force alter the force balance (magnetostrophic), and there is no atmospheric analogue of induction.

name: Rotating stratified turbulence
summary: Ocean and core flows both exhibit rotation-dominated turbulence with inverse cascades and large-scale coherent structures, offering shared numerical and scaling tools.
breaks: Core flows are electrically conducting with Lorentz feedback, absent in oceans.

name: Geodynamo and the liquid outer core
summary: Earth's magnetic field is sustained by convective dynamo action in the liquid iron outer core, whose structure and inner-core growth are constrained by seismology.

name: Seismic constraints on dynamo core
summary: Seismic models give core radius, inner-core size and density jump, supplying boundary conditions and energy budget for geodynamo simulations.

name: Alfvén waves and Rossby waves
summary: Magnetic tension restoring Alfvén waves parallels the Coriolis restoring force of inertial and Rossby waves, and both reduce to similar dispersion structures in rotating or magnetized media.
breaks: Alfvén waves are non-dispersive, while Rossby and inertial waves are strongly dispersive and anisotropic differently.

name: Turbulent cascades in anisotropic media
summary: Anisotropic MHD cascades and quasi-2D geostrophic turbulence both develop strong anisotropy and inverse or dual transfers under a strong organizing field or rotation.
breaks: MHD has forward energy cascade in 3D with critical balance, differing from atmospheric inverse energy cascade.

name: Space charge and beam plasma physics
summary: Intense charged beams behave as non-neutral plasmas with Debye length, plasma frequency, space-charge tune shift and Coulomb-crystal ordering in cooled ion beams.
breaks: Beams are non-neutral and lack quasi-neutrality, so screening and collective response differ from true plasmas.

name: Vlasov description of beams
summary: Collective beam dynamics uses the Vlasov equation in phase space, with Landau damping of coherent modes via tune spread, equivalent to plasma Landau damping.

name: Beam instabilities as streaming instabilities
summary: Two-stream, Weibel and head-tail or microwave instabilities in beams share the kinetic-instability machinery of plasma physics, including Landau damping used to stabilise bunches.

name: Ionospheric and radiative propagation in plasma
summary: Electromagnetic wave propagation in ionised media, with plasma frequency cutoff, underlies ionospheric reflection and remote sensing, alongside atmospheric radiative physics.

name: Adiabatic invariants and magnetic focusing
summary: Gyration, mirror trapping and adiabatic invariants in plasma map onto betatron motion, Courant–Snyder invariants and magnetic confinement in storage rings and traps.
breaks: Accelerator lattices use alternating-gradient focusing with no plasma-style collective response.

name: SRF cavities and superconducting magnets with SQUIDs
summary: Superconducting technology (niobium, cryogenics, flux control) is shared by accelerator cavities/magnets and SQUID sensors; SRF cavities also serve as quantum and dark-matter sensors.

name: Superconducting magnets in MRI and accelerators
summary: NbTi superconducting magnet and cryogenic technology developed for accelerators is the basis of clinical MRI magnets; both need field homogeneity and quench protection.

name: Cyclotron isotope production for PET
summary: Medical cyclotrons produce short-lived PET radioisotopes such as 18F and 11C, linking accelerator sources and targets to radiopharmaceutical supply.

name: Linacs and cyclotrons for radiotherapy
summary: Medical linacs, proton cyclotrons and synchrotrons, and superconducting magnets/RF are accelerator technology deployed clinically; the Bragg-peak beam delivery rests on accelerator design.

name: Radiotherapy demands on accelerator design
summary: Radiotherapy drives compact, reliable accelerator design: energy variation, FLASH dose rates, gantry-mounted superconducting magnets for proton and carbon-ion therapy.

name: Resonances and chaos in beams and fluids
summary: Nonlinear resonances, Hamiltonian chaos and dynamic aperture in storage rings parallel Rossby-wave resonant interactions and predictability limits in atmospheric flow.
breaks: Beam dynamics is conservative Hamiltonian; atmosphere is dissipative and forced.

name: Beam optics in proton therapy gantries
summary: Twiss parameters, emittance and focusing lattices determine spot size, beam transport and pencil-beam scanning in proton and carbon-ion therapy beamlines and gantries.

name: Synchrotron characterisation of battery materials
summary: Operando X-ray diffraction, absorption and tomography at synchrotrons track phase transformations and degradation in electrodes and solid electrolytes.

name: Free-electron laser vs. stimulated emission lasers
summary: FEL gain from SASE microbunching is collective stimulated emission by free electrons, analogous to semiconductor laser gain but without bound-state inversion.
breaks: FEL gain is classical bunching in an undulator, tunable and not tied to band gaps or carrier recombination.
